key_insight: Structurally constrained neural softening functions extend pseudo-elastic Mullins-effect models to capture composition-dependent stress softening while preserving physical admissibility.
engineering_relevance: The approach can improve constitutive predictions for filled rubber formulations while supporting more robust parameter calibration.
method: Embed parameter-dependent neural softening functions in a pseudo-elastic framework.
Use multiplicative softening decompositions to enforce mechanical conditions by construction.
Derive an enforceable sufficient condition for ellipticity and assess accuracy–constraint trade-offs.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses multiaxial experimental data from carbon black-filled EPDM rubber with varying curative contents to compare prediction accuracy and calibration robustness.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish generalization beyond the tested rubber formulations or quantify the gains from individual constraints.
paper_title: Constrained neural softening functions for the Mullins effect in parameter-dependent materials
